sanjay: Quick follow-up from the RFC — thinking about a small focused change to the private edge connector handoff semantics for Dedicated/private customers. goal: reduce cross-account NAT churn during cutovers and make graceful drain explicit. :eyes:

marta: high level sketch?

sanjay: idea is a 3-phase handoff: 1) announce-prep (routeWeight=80, maintain srcip preservation), 2) drain-window (accept new conns but prefer existing paths for srcip preservation), 3) commit (routeWeight=100, old connector marks DECOMMISSION). This is per-tenant and per-az.

olivia: routeWeight as a knob sounds useful. how does this interact with customers using static routes vs privatelink?

sanjay: for privatelink endpoints we rely on DNS / LB weights. for customers on static routing/peering we emit a weighted route update via controller and push a small lambda to peer-owner to adjust local preference. if peer-owner can't accept weight, fallback to timed cutover with connection drain heuristics.

ryan: runtime concerns: when we reduce weight, we still need to keep kv-cache warm for active sessions. suggest connector keep a short lived kv-cache proxy during drain-window until all active sessions idle or timeout. we ran into token exchange latencies previously.

marta: agree, kv-cache preservation is key for chat sessions. what's the proposed timeout? customers with long LLM sessions could keep conn open for minutes.

sanjay: propose default drain-window 120s with a per-customer override up to 1200s. also expose `handoffGraceMs` in connector policy.

olivia: security question — cert rotation and ephemeral tokens: during the prep phase do we exchange new certs or keep existing? wanted to avoid momentary mismatches.

sanjay: keep existing certs valid for hgrace window then rotate post-commit. ephemeral token exchange uses an ephemeral-proxy handshake: connector A stamps a short-lived claim that connector B can accept. infra-bot will bake audit logs.

infra-bot: deploy-check: there are 2 failing infra tests that block config rollout to staging: connector-policy-schema-validation and e2e-handshake. run `make infra-test-connector` to reproduce.

ryan: thanks infra-bot. i'll take the schema fix. quick patch idea: add two new optional fields to the connector CRD: `handoffGraceMs` and `routeWeight` (int 0-100). default: 120000 and 100 respectively. lightweight validation and controller-side enforcement.

marta: operationally we need metrics: per-tenant `handoff_inflight`, `handoff_duration_ms`, `srcip_preservation_failures` and `connector_kv_cache_hits_during_handoff`. i'll add dashboard tiles.

sanjay: agree. also add alerting for >5% srcip_preservation_failures over 5m during a roll. that should catch broken peer hooks.

olivia: one more edge case: dual-handoff when both primary and backup get updated simultaneously (race). propose controller uses monotonic handoff epoch and only one active handoff per tenant. if conflicting handoffs detected, we prefer the one with higher `routeWeight` preference and notify owners.

ryan: implementation plan: 1) CRD shim + schema tests (small PR) 2) controller enforcement + route emitter (canary on staging) 3) kv-cache keepalive proxy and token claim flow 4) dashboards & alerts 5) gradual rollout. estimate 2 sprints.

marta: i'd like a doc blurb for customers (support playbook) describing how to opt-in/out and fallback to relay mode if their peering cannot accept weights.

sanjay: will draft RFC follow-up summary and a short runbook for support. also add a cutover checklist: `pre-check peering mutability`, `check cert TTLs`, `monitor srcip_preservation_failures`.

olivia: :thumbsup: thanks — sounds like a sane incremental improvement.

ryan: i'll open the CRD PR and link it here once ready.

sanjay: thanks everyone. ping me if you want to pair on the kv-cache proxy design.

infra-bot: note: scheduled staging deploy window tomorrow 03:00 UTC.

ryan: ack, will aim to have CRD PR up before then.

marta: added initial dashboard mocks to `/#dashboards/edge-handoff` — feedback welcome.

sanjay: nice, i'll review after lunch.
